items.title: Kimsuky attacks targeting Ukrainian experts in diplomacy, security, and international policy
items.content: The Kimsuky threat group has launched spear phishing campaigns targeting Ukrainian experts in diplomacy, security, and international policy through fraudulent international conference invitations and collaboration requests. items.title: The XG Files: Falcon C2 Flying Under The (Browser) Radar
items.content: A sophisticated command and control framework named Falcon (also known as XG or Xiàng Gē) has been identified operating entirely within browser contexts through malicious JavaScript. The framework compromises webmail portals and government web applications, enabling attackers to sideload malicious Chrome and Firefox extensions that steal passwords, emails, session cookies, and communications.... This pulse includes 26 indicators of compromise (IOCs). Targeted industries: Government, Defense, Telecommunications. Associated malware: Falcon, Antino.

items.title: SCKit Worm Installs Rogue ScreenConnect Clients and Session Cookie Relays Across Hundreds of Endpoints
items.content: On November 11, 2026, operators exploited cloud-hosted ScreenConnect panels to deploy attacker-controlled clients and the SCKit toolkit across 288 hosts in 48 organizations. ConnectWise disabled five third-party extensions as a precaution but had not identified the initial access vector. Associated malware: SCKit, RelayTrap.

items.title: The global socket: how threat actors are weaponizing GSocket for stealthy C2
items.content: Multiple threat actors have been deploying GSocket, an open source remote access tool, on compromised Linux servers to maintain persistent access even after initial vulnerabilities are patched.
